questions.title: Generic Storage Box
questions.objective: Write a generic class with a type parameter and use it with two different types.

Implement a generic class StorageBox<T> that stores one value of type T. It must have a private field, a constructor accepting the initial value, setValue(T value) to replace the stored value, and getValue() to return the current value.

Read a product name and an integer quantity. Create a StorageBox<String> for the name and a StorageBox<Integer> for the quantity. Update the name box using setValue() before printing both values.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The replacement name is stored in the string box. The integer box stores the quantity independently.

Second line: replacement product name.
Third line: integer quantity.

Product: <replacement name>
Quantity: <quantity>

Each name contains 1–100 characters and may contain spaces.
0 ≤ quantity ≤ 1,000,000

Read the names with sc.nextLine(), because they may contain spaces.
Create the boxes with new StorageBox<>(initialName) and new StorageBox<>(quantity); Java infers the type from the declaration.

questions.title: Least Recently Used Cache
questions.objective: Build an LRU cache with an access-ordered LinkedHashMap and removeEldestEntry().
questions.problem_statement:
Implement a generic class LRUCache<K, V> using an access-ordered LinkedHashMap<K, V>. The cache has a fixed positive capacity.

The class must provide:
- get(K key): return the stored value and mark the key as most recently used. Return null if the key does not exist.
- put(K key, V value): insert or update the entry. An updated key becomes most recently used. If insertion exceeds capacity, evict the least recently used entry.
- size(): return the number of stored entries.
Process commands in order. Keys and values are single tokens. GET prints the value or Not found; SIZE prints the current size; PUT produces no output.

Required technique: Configure LinkedHashMap for access order and implement eviction through removeEldestEntry() or equivalent logic. An insertion-ordered map alone is insufficient.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: Accessing A makes it more recently used than B. When C is inserted, B is evicted. Updating A changes its value without increasing the cache size.
questions.input_format:
First line: integers C and Q, representing capacity and command count.
Next Q lines: PUT key value, GET key, or SIZE.
questions.output_format: Print one line for each GET or SIZE command.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ C, Q ≤ 100,000
Key and value lengths: 1–50 characters.
sample_inputs:
2 8
PUT A apple
PUT B banana
GET A
PUT C cherry
GET B
GET A
PUT A apricot
SIZE

1 4
PUT A a
PUT B b
GET A
GET B
hints: The constructor new LinkedHashMap<>(16, 0.75f, true) orders entries by access instead of insertion.
Override removeEldestEntry(Map.Entry<K, V> eldest) to return size() > capacity; the map then evicts automatically after each put.
A failed GET must not change the order; LinkedHashMap.get() only reorders keys that exist.

questions.title: Emergency Ticket Priority Queue
questions.objective: Order a PriorityQueue with a two-key comparator that cannot overflow.
questions.problem_statement:
A hospital support desk processes tickets by urgency. Each ticket has an integer priority and an integer ID. A smaller priority value means greater urgency. If priorities match, the smaller ticket ID must be processed first.

Create a Ticket class and use a PriorityQueue<Ticket> with a comparator that compares priority first and ID second. Use Integer.compare() instead of subtraction to prevent integer overflow.

Commands:
- ADD priority id: insert a ticket.
- NEXT: remove and print the most urgent ticket, or print No pending tickets if empty.
ADD produces no output.

Performance hint: Buffer output in a StringBuilder.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: Priority 1 tickets come before priority 2. Within priority 1, ID 101 is processed before ID 110.
questions.input_format:
First line: integer Q.
Next Q lines: ADD priority id or NEXT.
questions.output_format: For a successful NEXT, print Priority: <priority>, ID: <id>. Otherwise, print No pending tickets.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ Q ≤ 100,000
Priorities and IDs fit in int.

questions.title: Sum Values From Any Numeric List
questions.objective: Accept lists of different numeric types through an upper-bounded wildcard.
questions.problem_statement:
Implement a generic method sum(List<? extends Number> values) that adds numeric values and returns the result as a double.

The wildcard bound must allow the method to accept lists such as List<Integer>, List<Long>, and List<Double>. Iterate over the list and use doubleValue() for each element. Do not create separate summation methods for each numeric type.

For this problem, support the input types INT and DOUBLE. Construct the corresponding list and pass it to the same summation method. Print the result with exactly two decimal places, using Locale.US.

Required technique: Use List<? extends Number> and Number.doubleValue().

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The sum is 40. The same wildcard-based method can process both integer and decimal lists because their element types extend Number.
questions.input_format:
First line: INT or DOUBLE.
Second line: integer N.
Third line: N space-separated values.
questions.output_format: Print Sum: followed by a space and the total with exactly two decimal places.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 100,000
Integer values fit in int.
Double values are finite and have absolute values no greater than 1,000,000.
hints: A List<Integer> is not a List<Number>, but it is a List<? extends Number>.
Inside the method, you can read elements as Number and call doubleValue(); you cannot add elements to the list.
Summing as doubles also avoids int overflow when large integers are added.

questions.title: Group Employees by Department
questions.objective: Write a generic grouping method that takes a key-extracting Function and returns a Map of lists.
questions.problem_statement:
Implement a generic static method groupBy that accepts a list of records and a function that extracts a grouping key from each record. The method must return a Map<K, List<T>>.

Use Function<T, K> from java.util.function. Create an Employee class containing a name and department. Group employees by department using the generic method.

Use a TreeMap for the returned grouping map so departments are displayed in alphabetical order. Employees within each department must remain in their original input order. Do not sort employee names within a department.

Import java.util.function.Function.

Required technique: Use Function<T, K> to extract keys and TreeMap to order groups.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The generic method groups employee objects by their department. TreeMap sorts department keys alphabetically while each department's list retains the employees' input order.

questions.title: Process a Task Queue Without Duplicates
questions.objective: Coordinate a queue with two sets to reject duplicate and already-completed tasks in O(1).
questions.problem_statement:
A job-processing service maintains pending tasks in a first-in, first-out queue and tracks completed tasks in a set.

Use ArrayDeque<Integer> for pending task IDs and HashSet<Integer> for completed IDs. Also maintain a set of IDs currently pending so that duplicate pending tasks can be rejected efficiently.

Commands:
- ADD id: add the task only if it is neither pending nor completed.
- PROCESS: remove the front task, mark it completed, and print Processed: <id>. If the queue is empty, print No pending tasks.
- PENDING: print the number of waiting tasks.
- DONE id: print true if the ID has completed, otherwise false.
A completed task must never be added again. A task currently in the queue must not appear more than once. ADD produces no output.

Performance hint: Use a StringBuilder for output.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes and interfaces without the public keyword.

Explanation: The second ADD 10 is ignored because task 10 is already pending. After processing it, a later attempt to add it is ignored because it has completed. Task 20 is processed next, leaving the queue empty.
questions.input_format:
First line: integer Q.
Next Q lines: ADD id, PROCESS, PENDING, or DONE id.
questions.output_format: Print one line for each PROCESS, PENDING, or DONE command.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ Q ≤ 100,000
Task IDs fit in int.

ADD 20
ADD 10
PENDING
PROCESS
DONE 10
ADD 10
PROCESS
PENDING
hints: Checking queue.contains(id) scans the whole queue; a pending set answers the same question in constant time.
On PROCESS, remove the ID from the pending set and add it to the completed set.
Collect the output in a StringBuilder and print it once at the end; printing 100,000 lines one by one can be slow.
